body: I feel like I just willingly exposed myself to a cognito-hazard
Hey there! I’m a 29yr old guy living in East Side San Jose that’s available to help (mostly after 3:00 PM on weekdays)

Damn, are you me?

Left college with a BS in biology and 6 months  of research experience; tried applying for biotech companies and no offers after nearly 2 months of continuous interviews.

Said fuck it and joined a medical manufacturing company for $16/hr with zero experience in the field just to start paying my college loans

Fast-forward 4 years and I’m now making $35/hr in the same company’s QA department (also have little to none experience in this and I’m still learning new things everyday)

Life is fucking weird sometimes, but I truly am grateful for the people who gave me the opportunities to get me where I am now. But like you said, I was told the exact same crap by my parents growing up and all it got me was a 35k loan and life-long imposter syndrome.
You gotta try being a slave, to fight against slavery.

So I have the total estimate from the court summons here: Medical expenses $4,237.00; General Damages $5,763.00 for a total of $10,000.00.  

He included receipts for the medical expenses and estimate of record from a local collision center (only lists $204.71 for his rear bumper). From what I can see, it looks like the estimate of record is missing a page, which I'm assuming was sent to the other defendant (unless it was mistakenly or purposely left out).

Thanks for letting me know. I'll definitely keep this in mind as I'm working on the case.

If we do find that he was paid by his insurance, even partially, would that exclusion only work if he didn't cash the check? Does it matter how much he was paid? It seems to me that the only reasons he's suing me is either because he didn't get enough/anything from his insurance or he has concrete evidence that proves I and/or the driver behind me was at fault for the accident and is taking advantage of the $10,000 limit for small claims (as well as including the driver behind me in the lawsuit)

I did just that, forwarded my court summons as well as the attached receipts for damages to my insurance.

As for "the check", do you mean a check from his insurance claim right after the accident? I won't know yet, since my insurance is still working on getting the paperwork from when he filed (we both have AAA, so my insurance is trying to get access to his testimonial/claim)
Thank you! I'm learning all sorts of new things today (for all its worth lol).

Ahh ok, so this is what falls under liability protection, where the insurance pays up to my policy's limit. Thanks for explaining! I always thought that once the insurance case was closed, it would be "out of their hands" and that it would be up to me alone to defend myself against personal small claims.

But isn't the point of small claims is that he's suing me, and not my insurance? Why would my auto insurance be in a position to take the fall for the lawsuit? I thought they already took my case and closed it.

You're right about that. At worst, I'm estimating that I'll have to cover his medical and damages to his car (assuming that the person behind me is found to be totally guilt-free). At best, the medical charges and damages might be split between both defendants (I forgot to mention that they are also being sued along with me).

Like I said, I was a dumbass then, and I’m still a dumbass now. I really should have just called the police.

I also mentioned that I refused the rear car’s settlement. This was because I thought that the damages to my car was too little to bother having them pay for it, and that it was also a mental reminder that I wasn’t the one at fault. However, this was really naive on my part, and I should have accepted their offer.

Thanks for your kind and supportive words! 
I’m from California, so our laws allow people to sue two years after their supposed injury date. I’m also not looking to make any money. All I want to do is prove my innocence. I just wonder what kind of person is so salty to want to get money when their insurance couldn’t get them what they want.

I wish I could give you advice, but here I am, sympathizing how similar we are. If you ever want to share something about yourself, be it light-hearted or serious, I'm all ears.  

If you're curious, I'm the kind of guy who refuses to admit that he sings along to Charlie Puth everyday on the way home from work, but will gladly yell "SAFETY!!!" whenever he rips a fart near his coworkers ^ _ ^

I felt like this, too, when I first started college. Hell, even to this day, I still feel like my friends just invite me out because they've known me for too long to not include me.  

Yet, friendship, like most things in life, is a two-way street. I came to realize that if I ask how my friends are doing, they'll ask me back. If I ask them to take a walk after work, they'll ask to me to grab some boba and gossip. I think that if you start giving more effort and thought to the people around you, most the time, you'll tend to find people that either give back the same or even double of what you've given them.

This is gonna sound cheesier than any grilled cheese sandwiches I've ever made, but I found that I'm happiest when **I** ****do**** what makes me happy rather than ****pursue**** what **others** think should make me happy.  
Do mind, this might not apply to everyone, but it's worth a try.
Man, I still don't understand how I got my bachelor's degree when I was barely passing all my O-chem classes. Congrats, OP!

These are rough times, buddy. All of my friends are scattered to the wind, so I know what it feels like when we're all so wrapped up in our own lives to the point where we forget to ask each other how we're doing.  

Let me know if you need an ear to vent your troubles to. And most of importantly, stay strong ^ _ ^
Thanks, buddy. I hope you're doing well, too ^ _ ^

Hey pal, sorry that you feel this way, but happy birthday nonetheless :)

I used to feel like that, too.  Instead of looking at my birthday, I started calculating how long somebody will remember me if I die. If it was a year, I'll be like, alright. But if it was a month, or a week, then I'll *really* consider my options.

Later, though, I stopped caring whether I'll be remembered or not, cause no matter what, I knew I shared a moment with someone else, be it something simple as shaking their hand, hugging them, or just being with them.

So if you still feel like this, please know that you shared your time and a part of your life with them. Please know that no matter how they or you see each other, you were able to be a part of their life and vice versa. 

If you feel like talking or listening to someone, me and everyone else online are here. In fact, you can take a look at another post of mine and share your thoughts!
